10) IκBα, IκBβ, and IκBϵ, on the other hand, contain six ankyrin repeats, preferentially bind p65 and c-rel proteins, and show a widespread distribution among cells.

11) Thus, promoter binding of p65, c-Rel and RelB is usually associated with gene transactivation xref , xref – xref .

13) Notably, only p65, c-Rel, and RelB harbor a transcription activation domain (TAD), whereas p50 and p52 lack this TAD, and thereby may repress transcription when they are not associated with p65, c-Rel or RelB.

14) The five members of the mammalian NF-κB transcription factor family are p65 (RelA), RelB, c-Rel, p105/p50 (NF-κB1) and p100/p52 (NF-κB2), which associate with each other to form various transcriptionally active homo- and hetero-dimeric complexes.

17) RelB forms transcriptional inactive complexes with the subunits RelA and c-Rel.

18) Complex assembly of c-Rel, RelA and RelB with their inhibitors, the I κ Bs, in the cytoplasm results in inactivity as the interaction masks the nuclear localisation signal of the NF- κ B family members ( xref ; xref ).

19) As p50 and p52 lack this domain, they need to form heterodimers with RelA, c-Rel, or RelB to activate transcription of target genes.

20) The vertebrate members include the c-Rel, RelA, RelB, NFKB1/p105 and NFKB2/p100 proteins that form homo- or heterodimers with one another and bind to similar sites.
